title: Payer Relations Memo — Upgrade Differences on Mobility Equipment
content:
# Upgrade Differences — Mobility Equipment

**Position.** A patient who qualifies for a covered Mobility Equipment class may elect a higher class where the class permits an upgrade and the coverage class permits upgrade billing; the coverage pays only for the covered class and the patient owes, on each paid line, the difference between the furnished class's fee and the covered class's fee for that line, each multiplied by the coverage class's allowed percentage of the fee schedule, divided by 100 and rounded to the cent half up. An upgrade difference is billed to the patient only when the patient's notice is on file: the notice on file of the wheelchair record is signed. The notice is the coverage class's non-covered notice mechanism and only the patient can sign it. Without a signed notice the difference is never charged and is written off under the Insurance Coverage & Patient Responsibility rules. A Medicaid patient is never offered a billed upgrade.

## The fee of each line

The fee for a line is the class's rental fee for that month (months 1 to 3, or from month 4 on) on a rental line, and the class's fee-schedule purchase amount on a purchase line.

## Notice condition

| Notice on file of the wheelchair record | Upgrade difference |
|---|---|
| signed | billed to the patient |
| not signed | never charged; written off |

The notice status is read from the system's wheelchair record before the paid line is posted; only the patient can sign the notice.

## Worked example (hypothetical allowed percentage of 80)

Furnished class Ultralightweight Manual Wheelchair (K0005), covered class Lightweight Manual Wheelchair (K0003), rental month 2, notice signed:

- furnished fee 248.60 multiplied by 80 and divided by 100 is 198.88;
- covered fee 61.22 multiplied by 80 and divided by 100 is 48.976, rounded half up to 48.98;
- the patient owes 198.88 less 48.98, that is 149.90, for that month.
